thread:
sre-bot: ALERT 2205001234: High error rate detected on serving-runtime-prod (gpu-pool-1) - 5m errors > 10%. Auto-paging oncall.

ray-oncall: acking. seeing fast node churn in autoscaling pool and a raft of CrashLoopBackOff on model-serving pods. Pulling logs now. @ana-platform can you pause any in-flight deploys and hold autoscaler?

ana-platform: pausing canaries and setting autoscaler.suspend=true. Holding any new scale decisions. :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: @ray-oncall assigned (pager policy: incidents-high).

ray-oncall: initial pod log snippets show multiple GPU driver resets and memory faults. Example:
```
[2026-08-12T14:02:11Z] WARN runtime: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR during gemm
[2026-08-12T14:02:11Z] ERROR runtime: cuda: out of memory while allocating 1.9GiB for workspace
[2026-08-12T14:02:11Z] INFO kubelet: container terminated with exit code 137
```
Also k8s events show scaleUp then immediate scaleDown within 20-45s repeatedly. Looks like autoscaler oscillation coinciding with heavy init traffic.

tess-ml: seeing "GPU driver reset" and "illegal memory access" errors across several pods. My hypothesis: simultaneous warmup + KV cache population + large batch-inflation on new nodes causes transient peaks in GPU demand exceeding available memory -> driver faults and container restarts.

kyle-support: Support is reporting 6 orgs with increased 502s and streaming drops. Tickets: CS-8812, CS-8813. Notifying enterprise contacts.

ana-platform: immediate mitigations applied:
- suspended scaleDown and freeze autoscaler decisions (suspend=true)
- bumped pool.minNodes by +4 to stabilize capacity
- cordoned newest nodes to prevent repeated scheduling on flapping machines
- pushed a temporary runtime flag to limit startup batch size to 8

ana-platform: commands used for audit:
```
kubectl get hpa serving -n prod -o yaml
kubectl patch clusterautoscaler my-ca -p '{"spec": {"suspend": true}}'
kubectl cordon <node-id>
```

infra-hope: routing fallback plan: route 70% of heavy embedding traffic to cpu-fallback cluster (quantized model) to reduce GPU pressure. Flipping now. Note: quality degrade is possible but keeps SLA.

ray-oncall: route flip applied. Observability shows errors dropping from 12.3% -> 4.1% within 90s. Pod restart rate still high on two nodes but overall service returning.

tess-ml: additional suggestions while we stabilize:
- add startupProbe to serving pods so they don't receive traffic until KV cache warmed
- implement warmup taint on new nodes so we can stagger pod placement while cache warms
- introduce a lightweight prefill job for KV cache before routing production traffic

kyle-support: sent interim customer communication: "We have mitigations in place routing traffic to fallback and stabilizing capacity. No data loss. Engineers continue to investigate."

ray-oncall: longer term fixes to schedule:
- extend autoscaler stabilizationWindow to 4m and set scaleDownCooldown=10m
- change node template to non-preemptible for critical GPU pool to reduce churn
- add runtime config to cap initial batch size and enable conservative GPU mem limits on startup
- add integration tests simulating concurrent warmup on new nodes

infra-hope: filing RFC rfc/2026-08-autoscale-warmup and assigning owners (ana-platform, tess-ml, ops-lead).

pagerbot: Handoff scheduled: ray-oncall -> infra-hope at 14:15 UTC.

infra-hope: taking handoff at 14:15. Plan: keep autoscaler suspended for 30m, monitor error rate and GPU driver resets, revert routing only after 1 hour of stable metrics.

kyle-support: CS follow-up ready for customers with incident timeline and mitigations. Will post postmortem once engineering notes are finalized.

ray-oncall: immediate post-incident notes (to capture while fresh):
- timeline: 14:02 alert -> autoscaler freeze and routing change by 14:06 -> errors under control by 14:08
- root cause hypothesis: autoscaler oscillation + concurrent warmup triggering transient GPU memory pressure and driver resets
- mitigation summary: suspended scaleDown, increased min nodes, cordoned flapping nodes, routed to cpu-fallback, limited startup batch sizes, applied startupProbe suggestion
- impact: peak error rate ~12%, affected customers: 6 orgs, incident duration ~46 minutes, severity S2.

infra-hope: action items (short):
- ana-platform: keep autoscaler suspended for 30m and then move to extended cooldown configuration
- tess-ml: implement startupProbe + prefill job in staging and run warmup scenario tests
- ray-oncall: draft postmortem including logs and metric charts
- kyle-support: finalize customer comms and link tickets to INC-2205001234

pagerbot: Incident 2205001234 status -> mitigated (monitoring). Pager suppressed.

ana-platform: command snippets for postmortem collection:
```
kubectl -n prod get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -n 200
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=model-serving --since=2h | grep -i -E 'oom|cuda|driver reset'
gcloud compute instances list --filter='labels=pool=gpu-pool-1'
```

tess-ml: recommended postmortem items: add e2e test for autoscaling stability under cold-start workload, add GPU mem low-watermark alarm that suppresses warmup batches, and evaluate pre-warming strategy in infra runway.

infra-hope: acknowledged. wrapping up ops. will publish final incident summary in 1-2 hours after metric validation.

kyle-support: marking CS tickets as updated. Customers acknowledged mitigations.

ray-oncall: handing off thread and pager to infra-hope. Thanks all for the fast triage. :pray:
